lines.say: In 2001, a Dutch cardiologist named Pim van Lommel published a study in The Lancet.
He followed three hundred and forty-four people who survived cardiac arrest. Sixty-two of them, about eighteen percent, reported a near-death experience.
Certain features kept coming up. Here are three.
shots: q: soft light through window dust

lines.say: One. Overwhelming peace. Not fear. Many said it was the calmest they'd ever felt.
Two. Meeting people who had already died, often relatives.
shots: archive: old family photographs faded (public domain)

lines.say: Three. A life review. Their life replayed, sometimes through the eyes of the people they had affected.
Years later, those who'd had the experience had changed more: less fear of death, more empathy, than survivors who hadn't.
shots: line art: two groups, 8 years later
